title: Landing Gear
intro: You can't stop, cut or push off a leg that can't take a landing, so this session starts there. You take the force in, then you give it back. If you haven't done any jump work lately, start here, before Off the Mark and Hard Stop. It's about ninety ground contacts in all. You need trainers or court shoes and a line to hop over, like a court line or a strip of tape. A court or a rubber mat is kinder than tile or concrete.
If a landing gets loud or sloppy, end the session there. In a tournament week, skip this and do Green Light from the Mobility list instead.

before.label: Not today
before.text: A sore ankle, knee, calf, hamstring, groin or Achilles, or an injury in the last month? Get it looked at first.

before.label: Stop and get it checked
before.text: A sharp pain, pain that spreads, numbness, swelling, a joint that gives way, or a sudden pull or pop.

before.label: Stop now
before.text: Chest pain, dizziness, a heartbeat that races or skips, or breathing that doesn't feel right. Get it looked at before you train again. Told to be careful with hard exercise? Check with your doctor first.

before.label: A day or two later
before.text: Far more sore than normal, or your pee goes dark? Get it checked the same day.

before.label: Past injury
before.text: Coming back from an ankle injury? Ask whoever treated you if landing and jumping are OK. Skip the Lateral Bound if you've ever torn a knee ligament.

before.label: Check the space
before.text: Four metres of clear, non-slip floor and nothing overhead you could hit, like a fan or a low beam. No overhead room? Skip the Countermovement Jump. No four clear metres? Skip the Lateral Bound. Don't make it up in reps.

before.label: Keep clear
before.text: 48 hours away from another hard session, and not the day before a match.

before.label: First time
before.text: Do about half of the Rebound and Springs blocks, with full rest. It still counts.

good: Jog easy, or march on the spot if you're indoors, until you're warm and breathing a little harder
Feel your legs loosen up with every minute
Drive the knee forward over your toes
Feel the stretch low in the calf and the front of the ankle
bad: Letting the heel lift or the arch collapse

good: Hold a wall and swing the leg front to back, then side to side
Feel the hip loosen up as the swing gets bigger
bad: Arching your lower back to throw the leg higher

good: Step wide and sit back into that hip, chest tall
Feel the inside of the straight leg stretch
bad: Letting the bent knee cave inward

good: Step long, drop the back hip, then reach the inside arm up to the ceiling
Feel the front of the back hip and your upper back open up
bad: Rushing the reach before the hips have dropped

good: Push the floor away through your heels
Feel your glutes squeeze at the top
bad: Arching your lower back to lift higher

good: Rise onto the ball of your foot, pause, then lower slowly
Feel the calf working, not just the toes
From tall on your toes, snap down into an athletic stance and freeze, as quietly as you can
Your hips go back and your knees soak it up
bad: Landing stiff-legged and taking it through your knees

good: From tall on one foot, snap down into a single-leg landing and freeze
Feel your hip and thigh catching the landing, not your knee
bad: Letting your knee cave inward on the landing

good: Dip fast and jump as high as you can
Feel the floor pushing back through your whole foot
Push off one foot and bound sideways as far as you can still land and hold for two seconds
Feel the outside of the landing hip catching you
bad: Letting your landing knee cave inward

good: Stay stiff through the ankles and bounce off the floor quickly
Your calves acting like springs
bad: Landing on your heels instead of the balls of your feet

good: Hop over the line and back as fast as you can, both feet together
Feel your ankles doing the work, with quiet contacts
